title: Quality-vs-semantic split: does quality transfer and semantic not?
why: Fuse/route the available scorers; decide where deterministic physics rules are valid
hypothesis: Quality sub-problems (dark/blur/overexposed/frozen/duplicate) transfer out-of-domain; semantic sub-problems (no-active-work/hands-not-visible) do not
method: AUROC of {good} vs {bad windows with reason in category} for rules (total/quality-only/semantic-only), frozen ensemble_v1, adapted Z3 model

title: Deterministic regime router: routed system vs single scorers
why: Choose the scorer per regime; report review/error
hypothesis: A descriptor router (resolution/fps/regime) recovers the best scorer per regime and beats every single scorer on mean-domain AUROC
data: IndEgo gold 150 + OOD-160 with E4 regime descriptors
method: Deterministic routers (fps, E4 profile, aspect ratio, quality-gate, rules-review) evaluated by AUROC + calibrated-band review/error

title: Rank-average fusion: adapted x frozen (x rules)
why: Does fusion reduce the ambiguous fraction at equal/better error?
hypothesis: Rank-averaging the adapted score with the frozen ensemble improves grouped AUROC and cuts the review band
method: Rank-average of per-domain rank01 good-scores; AUROC grouped bootstrap; calibrated [0.4,0.6] review proxy

summary: IndEgo LOCO: quality rules near-perfect (AUROC 0.957, 11/13 quality-bad REJECT), semantic hard (rules 0.775, frozen 0.821). OOD-160 has 0 quality-bad windows (all 22 bad semantic/other) -> quality transfer untestable; rules invert on OOD quality-only (0.312) and fire on 93/138 good; semantic OOD solved only by adapted (0.749). Hypothesis 'quality transfers, semantic not' not supported as stated.
decision: Treat the split as 'where each scorer wins', not a transfer law; route in-domain->rules/ensemble, OOD->adapted

summary: No single scorer wins both regimes (rules 0.822->0.427; adapted 0.684->0.759; frozen 0.834->0.566). E4 descriptors (fps/profile) catch only the 30fps OOD batch (OOD label windows are all 854x480). Aspect-ratio router = 0.822 in-domain / 0.759 OOD (mean 0.791), best of all; review 0.15/0.26. Content quality-gate is a negative (OOD 0.680).
decision: Adopt aspect-ratio routing as the best configuration; flag it as a dataset shortcut needing a real in-domain detector

summary: Rank-average adapted+frozen is a compromise not a win: in-domain 0.834->0.784, OOD 0.759->0.686 (paired OOD gain vs frozen +0.120 [0.04,0.20], vs adapted -0.073 [-0.16,+0.00]). Mean-domain AUROC 0.735 beats singles but < router 0.791. Does NOT cut ambiguity: OOD review 0.31->0.53->0.86.
decision: Do not ship fusion as the primary; ship the router (rules in-domain, adapted OOD). Fusion only if no regime signal
